commitResults.messageTitle: Rename Duke to Chione
commitResults.messageBody:
Give the chatbot its own identity instead of the template's
placeholder name: rename the class and file, and replace the
ASCII-art banner so it spells CHIONE.

Also fill in the student profile fields in AGENTS.md.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add greeting and exit messges
Add echo support
commitResults.messageBody:
Chione now reads user commands in a loop and echoes each one back,
exiting on 'bye'. Output formatting is extracted into printBlock()
so later increments can reuse the divider-wrapped reply shape.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for storing and listing tasks
Add ability to mark tasks as done or not done
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a Task class that owns a task's description, done state and
display format, replacing the plain strings used previously. This keeps
formatting out of Chione and gives Level-4's task subtypes a base class
to extend. Add mark and unmark commands that look a task up by its
1-based list number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for todos, deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce Todo, Deadline and Event subclasses of Task, each supplying its
own type icon and extra fields via an overridden toString(). Because the
list and mark commands go through Task.toString(), they needed no change
to display the new types. Dates are kept as plain text, as the
requirements allow at this stage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid user input with a custom exception
commitResults.messageBody:
Add ChioneException so bad commands report a specific message and the
conversation continues instead of crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to delete tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Switch the task list from a fixed-size array to ArrayList, which removes
the capacity limit and the separate counter, and renumbers the remaining
tasks automatically after a delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename remaining Duke references and declare AI usage
commitResults.messageBody:
Update the README to describe Chione instead of the Duke template, list
the supported commands, and acknowledge the use of Claude Code at AI-5 as
required by the course reuse policy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add save file format to the task classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Give each task a toSaveFormat() that renders it as one line of text, with
the subclasses adding their own type letter and extra fields on top of the
shared done flag and description.

Keeping this in the task hierarchy rather than in the code that writes the
file means a new task type can be added without the file writer having to
learn about it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Storage to persist tasks between runs
commitResults.messageBody:
Load the task list from data/chione.txt at start-up and write it back
after every command that succeeds, so the list survives a restart without
each command having to remember to save it.

Build the path with Paths.get so it works on any operating system, create
the data folder when it is missing, and treat an absent file as an empty
list so that a first run is not reported as an error. A line that cannot
be parsed is reported along with the offending text rather than being half
understood, so a damaged file cannot turn into a silently wrong task list.

Ignore /data/ in Git, as the save file is user data rather than source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
Store deadlines and events as real date-times
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the free text held by Deadline and Event with LocalDateTime, so
that a date typed as 2019-10-15, or 2019-10-15 1800 when a time matters,
is understood as a moment rather than kept as whatever the user happened
to type. It is shown back in a friendlier form such as Oct 15 2019.

Gather the three shapes a date takes -- typed, displayed, and saved -- into
DateTimes, so no task class has to know a date format and a change to any
one shape happens in a single place. The display format is pinned to
Locale.ENGLISH so the output does not vary between machines.

A date with no time of day is recorded as midnight and displayed without a
time. This means a task due at exactly midnight loses its time on screen; a
separate flag would avoid that, but it is not worth an extra field here.

The save file now stores dates in the same shape they are typed in, so it
stays readable and anything valid in the file is also valid to type.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add on command to list the tasks falling on a day
commitResults.messageBody:
Add "on DATE", which shows the deadlines due that day together with the
events running over it, including events that began earlier and have not
yet finished.

Each task answers occursOn for itself, rather than the command testing what
type of task it is holding. A plain todo has no date and so always answers
no, and a task type added later will be searched correctly without this
command being touched.

This is the point of holding dates as LocalDateTime rather than as text:
the question being asked is whether two moments fall on the same day, which
is a comparison of dates and not of spelling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Move the task list behind a TaskList class
commitResults.messageBody:
Wrap the ArrayList of tasks in a TaskList, so that operations belonging to
the collection live with it rather than being scattered through whichever
code happens to need them. Searching by date moves there as findOn, which
also lets the result be shown by the same code that shows the full list,
since it is a TaskList too.

The underlying ArrayList is no longer visible to the rest of the program:
asList hands out an unmodifiable view for code that only reads through the
tasks, so the collection can only be changed through this class.

Behaviour is unchanged; a scripted run of every command produces output
identical to before, byte for byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Move console input and output into a Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Gather every System.out and the Scanner into Ui, so that no other class
talks to the console. The wording and layout of every reply can now be
changed in one file, and the rest of the program can be exercised without a
console attached because it no longer prints anything itself.

Ui's methods are named for what has happened -- showAdded, showRemoved,
showMarked -- rather than for what to print, so the caller reports the event
and leaves the choice of words to Ui.

Turn Chione itself into an object owning a Ui, a Storage and a TaskList.
Threading a Ui through a chain of static methods would have been worse than
the static state it replaced, so the two changes belong together. What is
left of Chione decides which collaborator to call and in what order.

Load the saved tasks at the start of run rather than in the constructor, so
that the greeting appears before any complaint about the save file.

Behaviour is unchanged; the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Move command interpretation into a Parser class
commitResults.messageBody:
Gather every piece of knowledge about the shape of a command into Parser:
which keyword starts a line, where /by and /from split the arguments, and
what counts as a usable task number or day. The error messages travel with
those checks, so the advice offered for a mistyped command stays consistent.

This empties two classes of work that was never really theirs. Command is
now a plain list of the words Chione knows, with no parsing of its own, and
Chione is left deciding what to do with a parsed result rather than working
out what the result is.

Behaviour is unchanged; the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly,
and javadoc -Xdoclint:all reports no warnings across the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreOOP'
Let TaskList refuse a position it does not hold
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the range check on a task number out of Parser and into TaskList. The
list is the only thing that knows how long it is, so it is the right place
to decide whether a position exists, and the check can no longer drift out
of step with the list however the number reaching it was arrived at.

This also frees Parser from needing the task list at all, which is what
lets a command be parsed before there is anything to carry it out on.

get and remove now report an unusable position as a ChioneException, so Ui
reads through asList instead of asking for tasks by position: every
position it uses is known to be valid, and displaying a list should not
have to handle an error that cannot happen.

The wording of the message is unchanged, including its counting from 1, and
the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename the Command enum to CommandType
commitResults.messageBody:
Free the name Command for the class that will represent a command the user
has actually asked for. What the enum holds is the vocabulary -- the words
that may start a line -- which is what CommandType names.

This is a rename and nothing else. Identifiers such as readCommand and
handleCommand are single words to the compiler and are untouched, and the
scripted run still matches the baseline exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn each command into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Give every command a class of its own behind an abstract Command, so that a
command knows how to carry itself out instead of being carried out by a
branch of a switch somewhere else. Parser now returns one of these, already
holding whatever it needs: the task to add, or the position to act on.

Chione loses its per-command branch entirely and is down to a hundred lines.
It hands the task list, the Ui and the Storage to whatever command it was
given, and asks only whether that command ends the conversation. A command
added later needs no change to this file at all.

Parser's switch covers every CommandType by name with no fallback branch, so
a command word added to the enum stops Parser compiling until it is given a
command to produce. That was checked by adding one: the build fails with
"the switch expression does not cover all possible input values", which is a
far better reminder than an error at run time.

One AddCommand serves todos, deadlines and events alike, since what differs
between them is how they are read, not what adding one involves. Saving now
happens in the commands that change the list rather than after every command,
so listing no longer rewrites the file it just read.

Behaviour is unchanged; the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly,
and javadoc -Xdoclint:all reports no warnings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreOOP-Commands'
Put every class into a chione package
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the source into src/main/java/chione and declare the package, so the
classes are no longer loose in the default package. src/main/java stays the
source root, which is where the build tools added later expect to find Java
source, and the package is named for the program rather than for the folders
above it.

Update the README, which pointed at the old path of the file to run.

Behaviour is unchanged; the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Split the classes into chione.task and chione.command
commitResults.messageBody:
Twenty classes in one package had stopped saying anything about how they
relate. Group the ones that model a task into chione.task, and the ones that
represent a request into chione.command, leaving the program's own moving
parts -- Chione, Parser, Ui, Storage, DateTimes -- in chione itself.

The grouping is visible in the imports: a command class now states that it
needs a TaskList, a Ui and a Storage, which is a fair summary of what
carrying out a command involves.

Imports are gathered into one alphabetically sorted block per file. Javadoc
links that now cross a package are written out in full rather than importing
a class solely to satisfy a comment, which would leave an unused import
behind.

Behaviour is unchanged; the scripted run still matches the baseline exactly,
and javadoc -Xdoclint:all reports no warnings across the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Merge branch 'add-gradle-support'
Build and run Chione with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Point the build brought in by add-gradle-support at this project: the main
class is chione.Chione rather than the template's seedu.duke.Duke, and the
JAR that a later increment will produce is named after the program.

Nothing else in the build needed changing. It already targets Java 25, and
already carries the JUnit and shadow plugins that the next two increments
will use.

Delete two compiled .class files that had been left in the source tree by
earlier hand-run javac commands. They were ignored by Git but had no business
sitting next to the source.

Document the wrapper commands in the README, since the wrapper fetches Gradle
itself and a reader needs nothing installed to use them.

Checked by replaying the same scripted run through "gradlew run": the output
still matches the baseline exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Gradle'
Test the parser, the storage, the task list and the tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Add 96 JUnit tests across five classes, run by Gradle with the JUnit 5
support the build already carried.

The classes chosen are the ones where being wrong would be quiet rather than
obvious. Parser is the only code that sees raw input, so each command is
checked both for producing the right result and for refusing a malformed
line with the particular message that says what to type instead. Storage is
tested against real files in a @TempDir, because what tends to go wrong
there -- a missing file, a missing folder, a line that cannot be read -- is
exactly what a stand-in would only pretend about. TaskList is tested hardest
at its bounds, since that check is all that stands between a mistyped task
number and an exception thrown from somewhere that could not explain it.
DateTimes is checked for round-tripping: a moment written to the save file
has to read back as the same moment, or a saved task would drift each time
it was loaded. The task types are checked for both of their renderings.

Ui has no tests. Its output is already pinned line by line by a scripted run
of every command, and asserting the same strings again in a second place
would double the work of changing any wording without catching anything new.

Writing the parser tests turned up a comment claiming that the limit of 2 on
the /by split keeps a description containing " /by " intact. It does the
opposite: the split stops at the first separator, so the description is cut
short there and the rest is taken as the date. The comment now says so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-JUnit'
Package Chione as a runnable JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The shadow plugin came with the Gradle support and was pointed at this
project when it was set up, so "gradlew shadowJar" already produces
build/libs/chione.jar. This increment is about checking that the result is
actually usable and saying how to use it.

Checked the way someone receiving the file would: the JAR was copied on its
own into an empty folder and run there with "java -jar chione.jar". The same
scripted run of every command produced output matching the baseline exactly,
and the data folder appeared beside the JAR rather than back in the project,
which is the relative path from the saving increment doing its job for a copy
of the program that has been moved elsewhere.

Document that in the README, including the consequence worth knowing: the
task list belongs to the folder Chione is run from, so two folders means two
separate lists.

The JAR itself is not committed. It falls under the existing /build/ rule in
.gitignore, and is published through a GitHub release instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Jar'
Document the packages and check the documentation in the build
commitResults.messageBody:
Every class and public method already carried a header comment, so what was
missing was the level above: what each package is for and how the three fit
together. Add a package-info.java for chione, chione.task and chione.command,
each saying what belongs there and, more usefully, what does not.

Point out in them the property worth knowing about this design: a new kind of
task means two methods in chione.task, and a new command means a word in the
enum plus a class in chione.command. Neither touches the conversation loop.

Turn on every doclint check in the javadoc task, so the documentation is
checked by the build rather than by remembering to look. Verified by breaking
it on purpose: an @param naming a parameter that does not exist now fails the
build with "@param name not found", where before it would have been a warning
nobody read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring the code in line with the SE-EDU coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Checked the source against the standard rather than against memory. Line
length, indentation, tabs, trailing whitespace, brace style, wildcard imports
and unused imports were all already clean, so what needed fixing was smaller
than expected but real.

Comments are required to use American spelling, and four words did not:
serialisation, recognise, recognises and Recognising.

Method names are required to be verbs, and four were not. corruptedFile and
numbered become buildCorruptedFileException and buildNumberedLines, and the
two test helpers become buildSampleList and buildThreeDayEvent. Each now says
that it makes something, which is what all four actually do.

Record the standard in AGENTS.md so that code written from here on follows it
without the rules having to be looked up again -- including the spelling rule,
which is the one easiest to break without noticing.

The tests and the javadoc task both still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
"find book" shows every task whose description contains that text. The search
ignores case, using a fixed locale so that it gives the same answer on every
machine, and matches anywhere in the description rather than whole words only.
Only the description is searched: a deadline is not found by the date it falls
on, which is what "on" is for. An empty search is refused rather than answered,
since matching everything is what "list" already does.

The command classes made this cheap. A word in the enum, a class that knows
how to carry itself out, and a case in the parser -- the conversation loop was
not touched, which is what that refactoring was for.

findOn and find differ only in what is asked of each task, so the walk through
the list is now written once and the question is handed in as a Predicate. The
task still answers for itself, so both searches work for any task type.

Fourteen tests cover the new behaviour, including the cases most easily got
wrong: a different capitalisation, a match on part of a word, and a word that
appears only in a rendered date rather than in the description.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-JavaDoc'
Merge branch 'branch-A-CodingStandard'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-9'
commitResults.messageBody:
Two conflicts had to be settled, and only one of them was reported by Git.

Ui.java conflicted where both branches had changed the same lines: the coding
standard branch renamed the numbering helper to buildNumberedLines and reworded
its comment, while Level-9 inserted showMatchingTasks immediately above it.
Both sides were wanted, so the new method was kept and pointed at the new name.

TaskListTest.java merged cleanly and did not compile. Level-9 added tests that
call sampleList, and the coding standard branch had renamed that helper to
buildSampleList -- on lines the new tests do not touch. Git saw two edits to
different regions and combined them without complaint. The compiler found it
straight away, which is the argument for building after a merge that looked
like it went fine.

All 110 tests pass. Replaying the scripted run differs from the baseline by
exactly one line: the list of words offered when a command is not recognized
now includes find, which is the change asking to be made.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the coding standard with CheckStyle
commitResults.messageBody:
The coding standard has so far been kept by hand, which means a slip is only
caught if a human happens to look at the right line. CheckStyle can read the
same standard and fail the build instead.

Add the CheckStyle Gradle plugin, with the sample configuration for the SE-EDU
Java coding standard in config/checkstyle. Pin the tool version so a Gradle
upgrade cannot quietly change which violations are reported.

Fix the 76 violations the tool found in the existing code:

* Order imports as the standard asks -- static, then java, then our own
  packages -- with a blank line between the groups.
* Indent the bodies of the arrow switches in Parser and Storage, so that the
  case labels sit inside the switch rather than beside it.
* Wrap the lambdas in the tests so that an opening bracket ends its line rather
  than starting the next one.

None of these change behavior; the tests pass unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-CheckStyle'
Give Chione a window to run in
commitResults.messageBody:
Chione has so far only been usable from a console, which asks the user to know
the command words before they can start. A window can show the conversation as
it happens and keep the last reply on screen, which is a gentler way in.

Add a JavaFX front end, following the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial:

* Launcher starts the app from a class that is not itself an Application, which
  is what lets JavaFX run from a plain classpath.
* Main puts the window on screen and hands it a Chione to talk to.
* MainWindow and DialogBox hold the behavior; the matching FXML files under
  resources/view hold the layout, so the design can be adjusted in Scene Builder
  without touching Java.

To let one chatbot serve both interfaces, Ui no longer prints as it goes. Each
show... call now adds to the reply being built, which is collected in one piece
-- printed with dividers for the console, or handed over plain for a dialog box.
Chione gains getResponse(String), which answers a single line and returns what
it has to say, and the console loop is written in terms of the same method. The
words the user sees are therefore chosen in exactly one place, and the two
interfaces cannot drift apart in what they say or accept.

The goodbye moves into ExitCommand, since the window has no run loop to say it;
the console still says goodbye itself when the input runs out without a "bye".

The text interface is kept and is still worth having: it can be driven from a
script, which makes it the easier of the two to test against. It now runs with
"gradlew runText", as "gradlew run" opens the window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-10'
Let a caller add several tasks in one call
commitResults.messageBody:
Two places in the code repeat a call only to pass one more thing each time,
which is what varargs is for:

* TaskList#add now takes any number of tasks. A caller with one task writes
  exactly what it wrote before; a caller with three no longer writes the same
  line three times. Loading a saved list stays separate, since those tasks
  arrive as a list rather than as arguments someone wrote out.
* The save-file helper in StorageTest now takes one line per argument, which
  gets the escaped newlines out of the tests. What each test describes -- a
  damaged line, a blank one -- can now be read at a glance.

Add tests for the two cases the new signature introduces: that tasks given in
one call keep their order, and that adding nothing is harmless rather than an
error.

Ui#showBlock already took varargs and is left as it is. Nothing else in the code
repeats a call this way, so nothing else is changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Varargs'
